paraphrase: Nārāyaṇa alone existed — not Brahmā, not Īśāna, not waters, fire and moon, heaven and earth; from his meditation arose fourteen persons and a maiden; later from his forehead came the three-eyed trident-bearer, and his sweat became the waters in which the golden egg arose, from which came Brahmā.
Ṛbhu teaches seven stages of ignorance (seed-waking, waking, great waking, waking-dream, dream, dream-waking, deep sleep) and seven stages of knowledge.
'This one is our own, that one a stranger' is the reckoning of the small-minded; for those of noble conduct the whole earth is one family.
